policy_title: Build new social homes and end Right to Buy
stated: Provide 150,000 new social homes a year at social rents and end the 'right to buy' to ensure homes remain community assets.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push to: • Provide 150,000 new social homes a year and end the so-called ‘right to buy’, so that these homes can belong to communities for ever.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets social housing supply (150,000 homes/year at social rents) and preserves existing social stock by abolishing Right to Buy — a substantial, non-negligible effect on affordable housing availability and rent affordability.

Building 150,000 social homes annually represents a very large capital expenditure (tens of billions per year at any realistic per-unit cost), materially affecting whether spending is funded or borrowed and the debt-path sustainability indicator.

Social rents are well below market rents (roughly 50–60% in England); directing this supply specifically to lower-income households concretely narrows the material gap between richest and poorest via reduced housing-cost burden, with a clear distributional mechanism distinct from O1's supply effect.

membership_note: The policy's primary effect is on housing affordability (O1); the fiscal scale of the programme earns a real O12 verdict; and the below-market rent targeting to lower-income households earns a distinct O14 verdict on distributional grounds. No other fundamental clears the non-negligible bar: cost-of-living (O2) effects are subsumed within O1 as defined; O10 (ending RTB removes a statutory positive entitlement, not a negative liberty); O15 (community asset framing too indirect to pin to a specific indicator).
